kings1.3.p1.b1.text: Later, Solomon formed an alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt by marrying his daughter. Solomon brought her to the City of David …

kings1.3.p1.b2.text: And Solomon loved the LORD and walked in the statutes of his father David, except that he sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.

kings1.3.p1.b3.text: Now the king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there … Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on the altar there.

kings1.3.p2.b1.text: One night at Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream, and God said,

kings1.3.p2.b2.text: Ask, and I will give it to you!

kings1.3.p2.b3.text: And now, O LORD my God, You have made Your servant king in my father David’s place. But I am only a little child, not knowing how to go out or come in.

kings1.3.p2.b4.text: Therefore give Your servant an understanding heart to judge Your people and to discern between good and evil. For who is able to govern this great people of Yours?”

kings1.3.p3.b1.text: Since you have asked for this instead of requesting long life or wealth for yourself … but you have asked for discernment to administer justice— behold, I will do what you have asked. I will give you a wise and discerning heart

kings1.3.p3.b2.text: Moreover, I will give you what you did not request—both riches and honor …

kings1.3.p3.b3.text: Then Solomon awoke, and indeed it had been a dream.

kings1.3.p3.b4.text: So he returned to Jerusalem, stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. Then he held a feast for all his servants.

kings1.3.p4.b1.text: At that time two prostitutes came to the king and stood before him.

kings1.3.p4.b2.text: Please, my lord, this woman and I live in the same house, and I gave birth while she was in the house.

kings1.3.p4.b3.text: On the third day after I gave birth, this woman also had a baby. We were alone, with no one in the house but the two of us.

kings1.3.p4.b4.text: During the night this woman’s son died because she rolled over on him.

kings1.3.p5.b1.text: So she got up in the middle of the night and took my son from my side while I was asleep. She laid him in her bosom …

kings1.3.p5.b2.text: The next morning, when I got up to nurse my son, I discovered he was dead. But when I examined him, I realized that he was not the son I had borne.

kings1.3.p5.b3.text: No … the living one is my son and the dead one is your son.

kings1.3.p5.b4.text: No, the dead one is yours and the living one is mine.

kings1.3.p6.b1.text: This woman says, ‘My son is alive and yours is dead,’ but that woman says, ‘No, your son is dead and mine is alive.’

kings1.3.p6.b3.text: So they brought him a sword

kings1.3.p6.b4.text: Cut the living child in two and give half to one and half to the other.

kings1.3.p7.b1.text: Then the woman whose son was alive spoke to the king because she yearned with compassion for her son.

kings1.3.p7.b2.text: Please, my lord … give her the living baby. Do not kill him!

kings1.3.p7.b3.text: He will be neither mine nor yours. Cut him in two!

kings1.3.p8.b1.text: Give the living baby to the first woman. By no means should you kill him; she is his mother.

kings1.3.p8.b2.text: When all Israel heard of the judgment the king had given, they stood in awe of him, for they saw that the wisdom of God was in him to administer justice.
